description: Credential vectors for the reference refusal rule (Agent Capability Standard 1.2.0, sections 6.7 and 5.18.10): the check that refuses persist data and audit records holding a secret, in grounded_agency/state/redaction.py (Redactor.holds_credential), packages/acs-core/src/redact.ts (holdsCredential) and the plugin's hooks/secret_scan.sh (secret_in). Informative: the Standard defines what a secret is and that such data is refused; these vectors pin the credential shapes the three reference implementations recognise, so they agree, and the prose they let pass. Each vector checks `input` (a string or a JSON value) with `secret_values` registered: `expect.holds` is whether it holds a credential. A string input wrapped in a JSON value ({"todos": [{"content": input}]}) gives the same result. The shell scan reads text only, so it runs the vectors whose input is a string and that register no value. Example tokens in a provider's own format (a Discord bot token, a Stripe live key, a Slack webhook URL) are written with one character as a JSON \u escape, so that the file's raw text matches no pattern that secret scanning acts on (a host's push protection, the providers' revocation of tokens found in public code); a JSON reader decodes the escape, so the vectors test the same text.
